methods.name: Peer-Median
methods.skip_reason: insufficient narrow peer set in Robotics & Manufacturing (found 0 same-stage, 0 adjacent-stage, 0 similar-tier; need ≥3)
methods.rationale: 11 same-sector peers exist in Robotics & Manufacturing, but none of the narrow filters (same-stage / adjacent-stage / similar-valuation-tier) yielded ≥3 datapoints. Falling back to all-sector median would be misleading.

data.narrative:
Bubble Robotics is a private robotics and manufacturing company founded by Jean Crosetti and Patricia Apostol. The valuation universe comprises 11 same-sector peers: 1 public company (277810.KQ) and 8 private firms, including Divergent, Exotec, Locus Robotics, Generalist AI, and Bedrock Robotics. The company's current stage and prior funding remain undisclosed, limiting precision in peer stratification.

The peer-median approach, the primary triangulation method for early-stage private companies, is not applicable here. The analysis identified zero same-stage peers, zero adjacent-stage peers, and zero similar-tier peers meeting minimum data density thresholds (requiring at least 3 datapoints). While 11 companies operate in Robotics & Manufacturing, none cluster tightly enough by development stage or valuation magnitude to yield a defensible median. An all-sector median would conflate fundamentally different risk and growth profiles across the robotics landscape.

Without sufficient stage-aligned or tier-aligned comparables, quantitative valuation synthesis cannot proceed. The key uncertainty is stage classification: whether Bubble Robotics is seed, Series A, or later directly determines which peer subset becomes relevant. Absent disclosure of funding history, current metrics, or deployment scale, no reliable valuation range can be derived from the available comp set. Additional diligence on the company's revenue traction, capital raised to date, and strategic positioning within the robotics sector is prerequisite to meaningful analysis.
